title: COP31: UN Climate summit enters final phase with no deal in sight
summary: After nearly two weeks of negotiations, countries remain divided on how to fight global warming. A new draft declaration doesn't mention the phaseout of fossil fuels, the main drivers of climate…

image.caption: Negotiators are scrambling to bridge their differences with the summit poised to be extendedImage: Yasin Akgul/AFP

blocks.text: After nearly two weeks of negotiations, countries remain divided on how to fight global warming. A new draft declaration doesn't mention the phaseout of fossil fuels, the main drivers of climate change. DW has more.

blocks.caption: Negotiators are scrambling to bridge their differences with the summit poised to be extendedImage: Yasin Akgul/AFP

items: Diplomats and delegates from nearly 200 countries are meeting in Antalya, Turkey
A new draft deal omits any mention of how to phase out fossil fuels, in what campaigners call a step 'backwards' and a 'glaring regression'
Like in previous years, the climate summit is likely to be extended until a consensus is reached

blocks.text: These are the major developments from the closing phase of the UN's COP31 Climate Summit in Antalya, Turkey, on Friday, November 20, 2026:
IN DEPTH — Fossil fuels dropped from latest COP31 draft deal

blocks.caption: Protesters at the COP31 in Antalya Turkey calling for a phaseout of fossil fuels, the burning of which is the main driver of climate changeImage: DW

blocks.text: One of the most fraught debates at the UN climate talks in Turkey has revolved around the future of coal, oil and gas.
Now, all mention of fossil fuels has been removed from the summit's new draft agreement.
Learn more about why fossil fuels, the main drivers of global warming, were removed from the COP31 draft declaration in this report.
